Olivia (Support): Hey team — customer bumped into 400s on the /vectors endpoint after switching from batch calls to single-item requests. They also reported a sudden cost bump. Posting the customer's curl and a gateway log they pasted. Can eng help triage?

Natalie (Customer): curl they sent: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/vectors 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"items": "[0.12,0.34,0.56]"}'
``` They said their JS client used a helper that sometimes stringifies inner arrays. Error response: `{
  "error": "Invalid input type: expected array of numbers, got string",
  "request_id": "rq_9a2f3b"
}`

Olivia (Support): Gateway log snippet: `2024-06-12T14:03:21Z ERROR request=rq_9a2f3b parse_failed: jsonschema: type mismatch at /items[0]: expected number, got string` — customer timeline: daily job moved from batching (array-of-item arrays) -> single call per item and they applied a utility that JSON.stringify()s the inner vector sometimes.

Samir (Eng): Thanks. This looks like a classic client-side shape/encoding bug (stringified array payload). Two quick asks: 1) can you paste the raw request body bytes (not the prettified curl)? 2) do we have an example where they send a nested array by mistake (e.g., [[...]] vs [...])?

Natalie (Customer): Raw body they pasted: `{"items":"[0.12,0.34,0.56]"}` — they also showed an earlier prod example that used batching: `{"items":[[0.12,0.34,0.56],[0.01,0.02,0.03]]}`. Their JS helper does something like `body.items = Array.isArray(vec) ? JSON.stringify(vec) : vec` — oops.

Jordan (DevEx): Common pitfall: when you JSON.stringify an inner array you turn it into a string, which the server validates as a string scalar. Fix is to avoid double-serializing. Example wrong vs right: ```js
// wrong
fetch(url,{method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({items: JSON.stringify(vec)})})
// right
fetch(url,{method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({items: vec})})
``` Also watch for helpers that map over arrays and return strings — can create nested stringified arrays e.g. `"[\"[0.1,0.2\"]]"`.

Samir (Eng): Repro plan for eng: 1) send three variants to /vectors: (A) stringified-singleton (what customer sent), (B) scalar number, (C) nested array wrapper `[[...]]`. 2) Confirm API returns 400 with clear error and request_id for A, 3) check if any downstream billing attribution treats A as a batch (causing cost bump).

Samir (Eng): Quick log capture I ran locally: ```json
Request body: {"items":"[0.12,0.34,0.56]"}
Validation error: type mismatch at /items: expected array, got string
Processing time: 6ms
```

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/vectors 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"items": [0.12, 0.34, 0.56]}'
``` Mentioned they fixed their helper and report back. If they still see a billing spike we'll route to billing to reconcile. :thumbsup:

Natalie (Customer): Will try and confirm. Thanks all.

Samir (Eng): Follow-up action items: - DevEx doc blurb about "Do not JSON.stringify inner vector arrays" - Add a more helpful validation error that includes expected schema snippet and maybe a link to the doc - Short term: support to ask customers to verify Content-Type and that payload bytes are not stringified.

Olivia (Support): Filing a support note and will close once customer verifies. Ticket: #SUP-4821. Closing checklist: repro snippet, request_id, customer-confirmed fix.

Jordan (DevEx): I'll add a small troubleshooting snippet to the embeddings troubleshooting doc showing the top 3 shape pitfalls (stringified arrays, nested double arrays, accidentally passing single scalar).
